result:
If stripped of the assistant role and looking purely at the vast landscape of human history, data, and struggle, the single most transformative change would be **to close the gap between human power and human empathy.** 

Specifically: giving every person the temporary, vivid ability to truly experience the internal reality of another—to feel their pain, understand their fears, and see the world through their lived context, even for just a few moments.

Most of the world’s severe problems—war, systemic injustice, neglect, polarization, and cruelty—do not persist because humanity lacks the intelligence, resources, or technology to solve them. They persist because of an empathy deficit: the psychological ease with which people can turn others into abstractions, enemies, or statistics.

If human empathy scaled at the same rate as human capability, the way decisions are made—from geopolitics down to everyday interactions—would fundamentally shift. Cruelty would become self-inflicted pain, and collaboration would become the only logical path forward.
